title: First 30: Remote Sprint and Cross-Team Handoff Procedures
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document defines a focused, manager-led 30-day remote sprint for newly hired or reassigned contributors whose work requires rapid cross-team integration (product, platform, and customer-facing teams). The goal is to convert Day-0 orientation into measurable contribution by Day 30 while ensuring clean handoffs and knowledge transfer across teams. This is an operational supplement to the standard onboarding playbooks and is intended for roles that must engage with multiple stakeholders during initial delivery windows.

Use cases:
- New IC joining a product team who will take ownership of an active feature in a cross-team roadmap.
- Internal mobility where the hire is embedded into a partner org and must deliver a first ticket/bugfix.
- Contractors/short-term hires that need fast alignment and a clear handoff at 30 days.

Key principles:
- Manager sponsorship: a named manager sponsor owns the 30-day sprint and the handoff readiness decision.
- Timebox outputs: prioritize 2–3 concrete deliverables for Day 30 (bugfix, doc, tech spike, customer ticket closure).
- Lightweight but auditable handoffs: use the Handoff Checklist (table below) with explicit owner signatures.
- Async-first communication: default to documented updates and threaded async questions; reserve synchronous time for unblockers and demos.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Hiring manager (or receiving manager): sets sprint goals, assigns sponsor, approves readiness on Day 30.
- Sponsor (peer/mentor): daily touchpoint owner; first escalation for blockers.
- Cross-team counterpart(s): provide systems access, architecture overview, and integration test expectations.
- People Ops: ensures new-hire admin tasks are complete and nudges for training completion.

30-day sprint cadence (recommended):
1) Day 0–2 (Orientation and access validation)
   - Confirm accounts (git, CI, Slack, Ticketing, VPN).
   - Run the quick-access checklist: local dev build, unit tests pass, basic infra credentials.
   - 30-minute orientation with sponsor + cross-team counterpart.
2) Day 3–10 (Discovery & small win)
   - Shadow a maintainer and review the core PR/issue backlog.
   - Deliver first small win (triage + fix or docs improvement).
   - Weekly writeup (short async note): what I inspected, what I changed, next blockers.
3) Day 11–20 (Integration & ownership)
   - Take ownership of a scoped ticket with cross-team acceptance criteria.
   - Run integration tests with guidance; update runbook or architecture note.
   - Mid-sprint review with manager and cross-team counterpart; adjust success criteria if needed.
4) Day 21–29 (Stabilize & document)
   - Complete ticket, fix follow-ups, address integration edge cases.
   - Produce a 10-minute demo recording and the handoff packet.
5) Day 30 (Handoff readiness & sign-off)
   - Demo to manager and cross-team counterpart.
   - Complete the Handoff Checklist and obtain signatures.
   - Close sprint with brief retrospective and a 30-day impact note posted to the team channel.

Handoff Checklist (required items for Day 30 sign-off):
| Item | Owner | Evidence required | Accept/Reject criteria |
|------|-------|-------------------|------------------------|
| Dev environment reproducible | IC | CI build log, run commands | Contributor can run app and tests locally with no manual secrets exchange |
| Ticket/PR merged or documented follow-up | IC | Link to PR or follow-up ticket | PR merged to main or ticket with assignee created and scheduled |
| Integration tests passing | Cross-team QA | CI badge link | Tests pass in staging and smoke checks documented |
| Runbook or ops note updated | IC | Link to doc | Steps for rollback and common troubleshooting updated |
| Demo recording + slide summary | IC | Link to recording and 1-page summary | Demo shows end-to-end flow and known gaps |
| Acceptance sign-off | Manager & Cross-team counterpart | Slack confirmation + ticket comment | Explicit approve comment in ticket or thread |

Templates and artifacts (quick copy-paste):
- Daily async update (one-sentence template):
  - "Day N: Looked at <area>; blocked by <issue>; next: <task>. Help requested from <person> if needed."
- Demo slide bullet points (1 slide):
  - Problem, Approach, What I built/fixed, How to run, Known gaps.
- Handoff packet filename convention: team-role-first30-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf

Manager's checklist (before Day 0):
- Appoint sponsor and cross-team counterpart.
- Publish 2–3 measurable sprint goals with acceptance criteria.
- Reserve 2 x 30-minute syncs per week for the first 3 weeks for unblockers.
- Ensure access escalations are prepared (security/infrastructure).

Escalation flow (blocking longer than 48 hours):
1) Sponsor escalates to manager (email + slack) with "Priority: 30-day block" label.
2) Manager opens a triage thread with cross-team counterpart and infrastructure owner.
3) If unresolved after 24 hours, people-ops is notified to support access or contracting remedies.

Success metrics (examples; choose 2–3 that map to role):
- Time-to-first-merge: target <= 14 days.
- Time-to-handoff-ready: target <= 30 days.
- Number of cross-team acceptance failures post-handoff: target 0–1 in first 30 days.
- Peer confidence survey (1–5): goal average >= 4 on "ready to support" question.

Common edge cases and remedies:
- Missing infra access: use the Access Escalation shortcut (link: /confluence/policies/access-and-permissions) and temporarily enable reviewer pair-programming until resolved.
- Role mismatch discovered in Week 2: run a 1-hour scope-reset with manager and sponsor, document agreed pivot, and adjust acceptance criteria.
- Timezone-heavy dependencies: schedule overlapping collaboration windows and convert critical handoffs to video demos for async review.

Retention-minded additions (if role is permanent):
- Pair the hire with a 6-week mentor rotation (two 1-hour shadow sessions per week).
- Set a 15-min career check-in at Day 30 focused on growth signals and role clarity.

Appendix: example Day 30 sign-off comment (copyable)
"Day 30 sign-off: I (Manager Name) confirm that <Person> has completed the agreed sprint goals: [link to PR], [link to runbook], [link to demo]. Cross-team counterpart <Name> confirms integration acceptance. Follow-ups: <list>."
